page: Amazon Web Services m8id.large is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as a 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2162.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 33.96 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is limited due to the 2-vCPU configuration, as reflected in a multi-core Geekbench score of 2695.0 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 2158.88. Memory bandwidth benchmarks are relatively weak, with uncached read-only large block speeds at 22.4 GB/sec and write speeds at 15.48 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also fall into the lower performance tiers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8id.large offers a balanced entry-point hardware profile with dedicated CPU resources and high-speed DDR5 memory, alongside integrated local NVMe storage. This avoids the overhead of network-attached storage for temporary files. The server is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and development environments that benefit from fast local scratch space but do not require intensive multi-core processing or high memory bandwidth.
